chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the man who leases a house, then sub-leases it for more than what he leased it for. He (peace be upon him) said: 'That is not correct unless he makes an improvement in it.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sub-lease a rented house for a higher price in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of *ribat* (sub-leasing) by linking the permissibility of profit to tangible value addition, such as structural improvements or renovations. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on avoiding *gharar* (uncertainty) and ensuring that the price difference corresponds to actual enhancement of the asset rather than mere speculation on the leasehold right.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>

regarding the man who leases the house, then he sub-leases it out for more than what had had leased it for. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘That is not correct unless he innovates something in it (makes an improvement)’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘ Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “

About the case of a man who leases a house then rents to someone else for more than what he has rented for, abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘It is not valid unless he introduces something in it.’”
